words.linea.retomarAnfitrion.text: If the room empties, the host can resume the game saved on their device.

words.linea.compruebaWeb.text: Check that the host has this table open in Kunobi and that you’re using the online game link.

words.linea.compruebaKunobi.text: Open the page in a Space with live editing. The host needs to have Kunobi open.

words.linea.mismoColor.text: If two of you pick the same color, the second seat gets another free one.

words.linea.soloAnfitrion.text: Only the host can free seats

doc.reglas.md.text:
# Castillos · rules

With 2 to 4 players, you build a kingdom together, tile by tile. Complete castles, roads and hermitages, and plant your banners wherever they serve you best.

## Components

- **60 square tiles**: **12 river tiles** and **48 in the main deck**. Each edge is **wall**, **road**, **river** or **field**. Some castles carry a **shield**, and some tiles have a **hermitage** in the middle.
- **7 banners** per player, in red, blue, yellow and purple.

## Setup: the river

1. The **spring** starts in the middle of the table.
2. Shuffle the river tiles separately, without the **lake**, which is kept for the end.
3. Taking turns, each player draws a river tile and places it **continuing the river**. The river can’t turn the same way twice in a row, so it never doubles back on itself. On these tiles you can already place banners on castles, roads and fields, but not on the water.
4. When they run out, place the **lake** at the end of the river. Then play continues with the main deck, shuffled face down.

The river **scores no points**. It gives you a long landscape to start from, and it **splits the fields** into two banks.

## Your turn

1. **Draw** the top tile of the deck.
2. **Place it** next to a tile in the kingdom so that all its edges match its neighbors': wall to wall, road to road and field to field. You can rotate it. If it doesn’t fit anywhere, it is set aside and you draw another.
3. **Place a banner**, if you like, on the tile you just placed:
   - on a **castle**, as a **knight**;
   - on a **road**, as a **traveler**;
   - on the **hermitage**, as a **hermit**;
   - **lying down** in a **field**, as a **farmer**.

   You can only place it in an area that has **no banner in it at all**, even far away. But a tile can **join** two areas that already had owners, and then that area ends up with several banners.
4. **Score** any areas that have just been completed, even if another player completed them, and return the banners in them to their owners. **Farmers don’t come back**: they stay in their field until the end.

## Who gets the points

In each area, whoever has **the most banners** scores. **If there’s a tie, every tied player gets the full points.** If nobody has a banner in it, the area scores for no one.

## Areas during the game

| Area | It’s complete when… | Points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Castle** | the wall surrounds the whole enclosure, with no gaps | **2 per tile + 2 per shield** |
| **Road** | both ends finish at a junction, at a castle gate or at a hermitage, or the road loops back and closes on itself | **1 per tile** |
| **Hermitage** | all 8 surrounding spaces have tiles | **9** (its own and the 8 around it) |

If a road passes through the same tile twice, that tile counts only once.

## End of the game

The game ends when the last tile of the deck is placed, after scoring whatever that tile completes. Then everything still open is scored:

| Open area | Points |
| --- | --- |
| **Castle** | **1 per tile + 1 per shield** |
| **Road** | **1 per tile** |
| **Hermitage** | **1 + 1 for each neighbor** it has |
| **Field** (farmers) | **3 for each completed castle** the field touches |

### Fields

- A field is the continuous grass between roads, rivers, walls and the edge of the kingdom. Roads and the river split it. A road that ends at a hermitage doesn’t split it; the roads leaving a junction do.
- Whoever has the most farmers in a field gets **3 points for each completed castle** it touches. A castle that touches the field on several tiles counts only once.
- The same castle can score for several different fields.

The player with **the most points** wins. If there’s a tie, the victory is shared.
